summary: Rejected on two remaining cumulative privacy defects: new-ID call resume/link renews accepted legacy source-bearing task text using the new session clock, and full-source diagnostic recording masks future/overflow capture timestamps with an earlier history clock before validation. Earlier exception-envelope and typed exact-prompt findings are addressed statically by API-contract full-input scanning/default-deny generic diagnostics; summary proof/tombstones and removal of voice epoch metadata remain intact. The retained Build890 class-resolution failure is genuine and the new Keep annotations are appropriate at source level, with direct test36 owners audited, but no compiled/device success is claimed. Exact remote/local tree binding, 14-path scope, frozen179 and original36 journeys all pass independent source-integrity checks. Preserve exact Build898 evidence without treating tests as resolving these defects.

findings.detail: R5: Resuming an eligible saved call renews inherited source-bearing taskStatus strings. VoiceSessionController.resumeCall (152-169) copies latest.taskStatus into a new UUID with startedAtMs=now, then MainActivity (173-175) calls linkConversation, which clears the copied transcript while retaining taskStatus (VoiceSessionController 174-176). VoiceCallStore.save/sanitize (31-35,43-67) only finds prior by the new call ID and dates derived title/task text from that new startedAtMs; it does not preserve inherited source lineage. Given an accepted persisted/legacy task string "Opened Amber Notebook" captured at t0, resume at day89 and link the conversation; at t0+90 days the original call expires but the new call retains the copied task text until day179, including after reopen. Current accepted-action Runtime generally writes content-free tool names, so the source-bearing persisted/legacy task precondition is explicit; the public store/codec and privacy contract nevertheless accept and cover arbitrary task strings. Content-free identity/outcome preservation can remain allowed. Keep derived-source provenance separate from session start across new-ID resume and the later transcript-clearing checkpoint, or fail closed for unprovenanced inherited freeform tasks. Repair can live in allowed VoiceCallStore without editing frozen controller/activity. Add a boundary regression that saves eligible prose tasks, follows resume+link, advances to original expiry, and reopens. Evidence: privacy-review-4-retention-probe.json is an exact source-level lifecycle model, not a Kotlin run.

R6: recordSourceInferencePrompt (lines 33-37) computes sources.minOfOrNull { minOf(it.capturedAtMs, sourceTimestamp()) } before validation. It then passes only that derived clock and source text strings to wrap/Privacy.placeholder, losing each source’s original clock. With clock/sourceTimestamp=1000 and a benign FullSource capturedAtMs=1001 (future) or Long.MAX_VALUE (overflowing expiry), the method produces captured=1000 and persists/binds the payload, even though Privacy.eligible rejects the original capture time. The supplied voice FullSource API must reject every missing/future/overflow/expired original clock before choosing the oldest eligible clock; an earlier history timestamp is not proof of that source’s capture provenance. This violates the explicit fail-closed invalid-clock requirement. The reduced clock is conservative for age but still masks invalid source provenance. The current full-source test covers valid epoch timestamps and secret text, not invalid clocks. Evidence: privacy-review-4-clock-probe.json evaluates the exact source arithmetic; no Kotlin execution claimed.
